title: cairn question withdraw closes a duplicate question unanswered
intention: cairn question gains a withdraw verb: withdraw <qid> --duplicate-of <qid> --why resolves an open question that duplicates another on the same ticket, carrying no answer and a withdrawn record naming the question that stands.
why: Measured 2026-11-16: Q#119 on e56a68e651c2 and Q#116 on 312be610152e each stood twice (one hand-opened, one opened by cairn outlinecheck), both copies held BUILDME, and the door's verbs (open operator answer note rebind list show) offered no way out but answering one. e1d3fd0f2aab (PROVED 2026-11-16) stopped outlinecheck opening the second copy; a question opened twice by hand still cannot be closed. The trouble question-has-no-withdraw-verb-for-a-duplicate stands live for it.
traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth stays true. A duplicate standing open tells the inbox and the BUILDME lane a decision is owed twice, and the only way to close it, answering, writes a decision nobody made.
how: Add withdraw(qid, *, duplicate_of, why, root=None) to cairn/tools/question/question.py: refuse (every lack named, nothing written) a blank why, an already-resolved qid, a duplicate_of that is itself, missing, on another ticket, or itself withdrawn; else write resolved=True, answer=None, spawned=[], withdrawn={duplicate_of, why, by, at} through the door with verb answer. Add the withdraw subparser to cairn/tools/question/__main__.py. Proof: cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_a_duplicate_question_is_withdrawn_unanswered.py (clauses 1-3). After PROVED, clear the trouble through ModuleRaiser('question').

clauses.claim: withdraw resolves the duplicate with answer None and withdrawn.duplicate_of naming the kept question, and open_for(ticket) lists only the kept one
a withdrawal naming another ticket's question, itself, a missing one, a withdrawn keeper, an already-resolved qid, or a blank why is refused and leaves the record's bytes unchanged
python3 -m cairn.tools.question withdraw <qid> --duplicate-of <qid> --why ... withdraws it from the shell, exit 0

decisions.text: D1: a withdrawal resolves without answering: resolved=True so the BUILDME lane (open_for) stops counting it, answer=None so corrosion's citation check and rung 4 cannot read it as a decision, and withdrawn names the question whose answer is the decision.
D2: the shell verb is a thin subparser beside note and rebind; --duplicate-of and --why are required.
D3: the proof is red-first in a scratch commons under scratch diagnostic roots (the test_question_links.py world).

out: cairn/machines/corrosion/citation.py (read, unchanged: answer None already refuses)
